title: Accounts Payable Assistant - Ongoing Temp - Hybrid
description:
Accounts Payable Clerk (Ongoing Temporary Assignment)

Location: Glasgow (Hybrid/Office-Based)

Pay Rate: £14.50 per hour

Hours: 40 hours per week

Contract: Ongoing Temporary Assignment

Start Date: Immediate

The Opportunity

Reed Accountancy are delighted to be supporting a leading multinational organisation in their search for an experienced Accounts Payable Clerk to join their finance team on an ongoing temporary basis.

This is an excellent opportunity for an AP professional who thrives in a fast-paced, high-volume environment and enjoys working as part of a busy shared service function. - Strong understanding of end-to-end AP processes
- Experience dealing with multi-currency invoices would be highly advantageous
- Confident handling complex supplier queries and reconciliations
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy
- Excellent organisational and communication skills
- Ability to prioritise workloads effectively in a fast-paced environment
- Proficient in Microsoft Excel and finance systems

What's on Offer
- £14.50 per hour
- 40-hour working week
- Immediate start available
- Ongoing temporary assignment with potential for longer-term opportunities
- Experience working within a well-established multinational organisation
- Supportive and collaborative finance team environment

If you are an experienced Accounts Payable professional available at short notice and looking for your next opportunity within a busy and dynamic finance function, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now or contact Reed Accountancy for further information.

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
Hybrid (1 day per week on-site, max 2 days when fully integrated) Free parking

The Payroll Administrator will provide vital business-as-usual (BAU) support to ensure the smooth operation of high-volume payrolls during a major system transition. The organization is currently preparing to migrate from iTrend to Oracle in April/May 2027. You will be responsible for processing multiple payroll runs and managing complex pension schemes.

Key Deliverables
Act as a key payroll focal point to support the team through a critical system migration from iTrent to Oracle.
Deliver consistent, high-volume BAU payroll processing for approximately 5,000 staff across 3 monthly payrolls.
Administer and coordinate complex pension schemes, specifically managing Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS) and Teachers' Pensions.
Resolve complex pay and pension queries in an efficient and timely manner to support employee wellbeing and engagement.
Manage the payroll workflow end-to-end, including processing new starters, leavers, structural changes, and contract variations.
Receive, verify, and input employee absence, sickness, and statutory payment records.
Process holiday requests, overtime claims, and manual payroll adjustments for payment processing.
Investigate and correct timesheet and payment errors, escalating system anomalies as required.
Maintain accurate and detailed logs of all personnel queries and payroll adjustments to ensure robust audit trails during the transition period.

Key Requirements / Qualifications
Education: Relevant payroll qualification (CIPP or equivalent) or demonstrated capability via extensive hands-on experience.
IT Skills: Solid IT skills across the MS Office Suite, including strong Excel and data analysis capabilities.
Experience: Previous experience managing high-volume payrolls within a complex, multi-payroll environment. Experience handling roughly 5,000 records across multiple monthly cycles is highly advantageous.
System Knowledge: Prior experience utilizing iTrent or Oracle payroll software is highly desirable, though not strictly non-negotiable.
Pension Knowledge: Demonstrable experience working with public sector pension schemes, specifically LGPS and Teachers' Pensions, is highly preferred.
Industry Knowledge: Previous experience working within a College, University, Local Council, or broader Public Sector environment is highly desirable.
Communication: Clear and confident communicator at all levels, capable of explaining complex payroll and pension queries face-to-face, via email, and over the telephone.

title: Credit Controller
company: Three Bridges Recruitment LTD - Agency - Permanent
description:
Location: Glasgow or Edinburgh (Hybrid 2-3 days WFH)

Salary: £32,000 + Exceptional Benefits

Three Bridges Recruitment has partnered with a prestigious, independent Scottish legal firm to appoint a Credit Controller to their Glasgow team.

This isn't high-volume, automated call-centre chasing. You will work collaboratively with partners and directly alongside an approachable Credit Control Manager, you will take ownership of a varied ledger, build trust with senior Partners, and help drive commercial collection strategies across corporate and private client accounts.

Why you'll love it?
- Work-Life Balance: 33.45-hour working week with a generous 1h 15m daily lunch break.
- Flexible Hybrid Working: 2-3 days from home per week once settled and trained.
- Collaborative Culture: Work with Partners as commercial stakeholders, advising on risk and tailored recovery plans.
- Top-Tier Benefits: 7% employer pension, 24 days' holiday + 7 bank holidays (buy up to 6 extra days), Health cash plan, car salary sacrifice scheme, Future Discretionary Bonus.
- Genuine Autonomy & Influence: Collaborative ledger reviews with partners where you are empowered to challenge senior stakeholders, advise on risk, and set collection strategy.
- Expanding, Dynamic Brand: Be part of a forward-thinking group integrating established legal brands, offering genuine career development and long-term stability.

About The Role?

Reporting to the Credit Control Manager and working closely with local stakeholders in Edinburgh, you will take full charge of day-to-day credit management and working capital optimisation:
- Ledger Ownership: Manage an allocated debtor ledger across diverse, high-value client accounts, proactively securing timely cash collections.
- Partner Engagement: Conduct structured, regular ledger reviews directly with Partners and Senior Associates, establishing agreed action plans and tailored recovery strategies.
- Stakeholder & Client Relations: Act as a brand ambassador, navigating sensitive or complex discussions with clients and tailoring your approach to preserve long-term commercial relationships.
- Query & Dispute Resolution: Investigate billing discrepancies and legacy aged-debt matters end-to-end, liaising with internal legal teams to unblock payments.
- DSO & Performance Management: Track and report on key credit metrics, contributing to ambitious group targets to reduce debtor days and mitigate bad debt risk.
- Process Improvement: Actively identify efficiencies across systems, billing flows, and collection processes within an integrating business.

About You?

We are looking for a commercially minded, resilient credit professional with a strong personality who can combine ledger competence with strong interpersonal skills:
- Experience: Proven track record in credit control, collections, or accounts receivable. Experience within legal, accountancy, or wider professional services is advantageous, though strong commercial B2 B backgrounds are welcomed.
- Communication & Backbone: Confident dealing with senior stakeholders and Partners; comfortable challenging constructively, negotiating tactfully, and holding firm on credit policy.
- Analytical & Organised: Skilled in ledger reconciliations, dispute resolution, and managing multi-matter billing structures with high attention to detail.
- Adaptable Approach: Ability to adjust communication style across diverse client sectors and handle sensitive accounts with discretion and diplomacy.

Apply

At Three Bridges Recruitment, two of our core values are "striving for brilliance" and "relatability." We want every applicant to have an excellent experience and ensure this opportunity genuinely aligns with your personal and professional ambitions.

If this role sounds like the right next step in your career, please apply with your CV or contact Ryan Strachan at Three Bridges Recruitment for a confidential discussion.

title: Finance Officer - Glasgow - Part-Time
company: Three Bridges Recruitment LTD - Agency - Permanent
description:
Finance Officer

£40,000 FTE (pro rata) 21 hours per week Hybrid Glasgow

A finance role offering the flexibility you want, the responsibility you enjoy and a cause worth being part of.

Good part-time finance opportunities aren't always easy to find, particularly those offering genuine ownership, a supportive environment and the chance to contribute beyond the day-to-day numbers.

That's what makes this opportunity with a well-established Scottish charity worth exploring.

Working alongside a network of community organisations across Scotland, our client uses the power of sport to improve health, tackle poverty, build skills and bring people together.

It's an ambitious mission, and a well-run finance function plays an important part.

The opportunity

You'll take ownership of the charity's day-to-day finances, working closely with the Chief Executive and a small, supportive team.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Managing transactions, payments and reconciliations using Sage 50.
- Preparing financial reports, budgets and forecasts.
- Monitoring project finances, including restricted and unrestricted funds.
- Supporting the integration of financial processes following a recent merger.
- Liaising with external accountants, auditors and payroll providers.

It's a hands-on role offering independence, variety and the chance to contribute as the organisation develops.

What we're looking for

You'll have solid bookkeeping or finance experience, ideally within a charity or not-for-profit organisation, and a good understanding of charity accounting.

You don't need to be a qualified accountant. Being organised, dependable, comfortable taking ownership and enjoying teamwork matters more.

An appreciation of the positive impact community-focused organisations can have is equally important.

Why consider it?

You'll enjoy flexibility in how your 21 hours are worked, hybrid working, pension contributions, healthcare cover, a family-friendly environment and a two-week Christmas closure.

You'll also join a welcoming team where people are trusted, supported and encouraged to contribute.

Interested?

At Three Bridges Recruitment, two of our values are "striving for brilliance" and "relatability". We want every applicant to receive an excellent experience and feel confident a role is genuinely right for them.

If you're an experienced finance professional seeking flexibility without sacrificing responsibility, and the chance to support a worthwhile cause, we'd be delighted to hear from you.

Please apply with your most up-to-date CV or contact us for a confidential discussion.

title: Part Time Payroll Assistant
company: Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Your new company

Our client is an established Glasgow-based organisation offering an excellent opportunity for an experienced Payroll Administrator to join their team on a part-time basis. You'll work 22.5 hours across three days, with a flexible hybrid arrangement of one day in the office and two days from home. The organisation is currently developing its payroll processes, making this a great opportunity to join during a period of positive change and contribute ideas along the way.

Your new role

As Payroll Administrator, you will support the accurate and timely delivery of payroll across UK and Ireland employees. Working as part of an experienced team, you will be responsible for a varied workload including:
- Processing payroll across multiple pay cycles
- Calculating statutory payments including SSP, SMP and SPP
- Supporting pension administration and auto-enrolment
- Maintaining accurate payroll records and completing regular checks
- Supporting year-end processes including P60s, P11 Ds and HMRC submissions
- Handling payroll queries from employees and internal stakeholders
- Working closely with HR, Finance and operational teams to resolve discrepancies
- Supporting payroll reporting and data analysis
- Identifying opportunities to improve existing payroll processes
- Assisting with system and process changes as the payroll function continues to develop

What you'll need to succeed

You will ideally have previous experience working within a busy payroll environment and be confident managing detailed payroll information accurately.

You will also have:
- Previous payroll administration experience
- Good knowledge of UK payroll legislation
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy
- Confidence working across Excel, including formulas and lookups
- Strong communication and problem-solving skills
- The ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines
- A proactive approach and willingness to improve processes

What you'll get in return

You will receive a flexible working arrangement of three days per week (22.5 hours), with one office-based day and two days working from home. This is a great opportunity to join an established organisation, develop your payroll experience and play a part in improving existing processes.

What you need to do now

If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call us now.
If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion about your career.
